claims.title: Log-free Kaczmarz best-iterate projection bound
claims.claim: For consistent real Ax=b and epsilon>0, max-normalized-residual greedy row projections produce an iterate in k<=ceil(||A||_F^2/epsilon^2)-1 steps satisfying ||Ay_k-b||<=epsilon||y0-x|| and ||y_k-x||<=||y0-x||; unscaled source-matched theorem to Steinerberger Theorem 1. General best-prefix inequality min_{t<K}||Ay_t-b||<=||A||_F||y0-x||/sqrt(K). Abstract scaled case yields k<=ceil(n/epsilon^2)-1.
assumptions: consistent real linear system with A nonzero, zero rows skipped
each iteration chooses a row with maximal squared normalized residual
orthogonal projections; one selected iterate among the first K, not necessarily the final iterate
claims.mechanism: Projection Pythagoras gives a per-step decrease; max normalized residual dominates its row-norm weighted average; telescoping bounds the sum of squared residuals, so one prefix iterate meets the threshold.
claims.evidence: Elementary complete analytical Pythagorean/weighted-maximum/telescoping proof, exact seeded checker 240 systems x12=2,880 updates, plus independent exhaustive 6,552 small systems x8=52,416 exact-rational updates; tests do not prove novelty.
claims.source_detail: Revision 1.1 source-matched unscaled Theorem 1 proof PROOF.md; exact_audit.py plus independent_exhaustive_audit.py. Historical checkpoint c3e4806e remains original provenance, newer revision is traceable in Git history.

claims.title: Exact consecutive 4-shuffle forcing threshold (N4 = 20)
claims.claim: Every permutation of length 20 has a consecutive factor of length 8 or 12 partitionable into four equal-size subsequences with a common relative-order pattern. A concrete length-19 permutation avoids every eligible factor (length 8, 12, 16), so N4=20.
assumptions: distinct permutation entries and standardization of consecutive factors
four disjoint increasing-index subsequences of identical pattern and size at least two
ordinary k=4 shuffle definition, not the conjecture for all k
claims.mechanism: Perfect-matching classification of 8-patterns; 5040-state avoidance factor graph with 2632 edges; all 302 twenty-position bad-eight paths force a 12-entry common-triple exact cover using only local comparisons; independently checked 19-term witness.

claims.title: Exact nested-address adaptive–nonadaptive separation
claims.claim: For an s-address m-ary replica with m^s fair-sign leaves, fixed c-query explained variance is g(c)=0 at c=0, m^(c−1−2s) for 1≤c≤s+1, then min{1,(c−s)/m^s}. For r outputs with k replicas, L=s+m^s and Q'=min(Q,rkL), a=floor(Q'/L), b=Q' mod L, the exact optimal fixed-query Bayes risk equals 1/k−(a+g(b))/(rk²).
assumptions: Uniform independent m-ary address symbols and independent fair-sign leaves
Whole-coordinate fixed nonadaptive query sets, conditional-mean squared-loss risk
Independent scaled replicas and outputs
claims.mechanism: Conditional fiber averaging gives gain q/m^(2s−h). The discrete-convex single-replica gain makes complete-replica concentration optimal by budget exchange; adaptive reading follows each address.
